iconicAnchor.label: Color Decoded: The Textiles of Richard Landis
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Cooper Hewitt describes balanced systems where rectangles, scales, tonal relationships, and color combinations repeat in ever-changing order.

sources.title: Color Decoded: The Textiles of Richard Landis
supports: Controlled variation can make repeating geometry appear lively while remaining balanced and systematic.

sources.title: Pattern Papers
supports: A repeat motif must be designed as part of a seamless larger surface with rhythmic positive and negative space.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches seamless repeat, motif family, controlled variation, scale shift, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/pattern-playground/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
